title: Why Arlington Condos Near the Potomac Get Musty Ducts in Summer
headline: Why Arlington Condos Near the Potomac Get Musty Ducts in Summer
description: River humidity, stacked laundry, and cool metal trunks: how Arlington HVAC systems collect moisture film — and when to schedule duct or dryer vent cleaning.

sections.heading: The moisture trap inside your air ducts
paragraphs: In a Virginia summer the air conditioner runs for hours. Cold air traveling through metal ductwork meets warm, humid air already in the building. The temperature drop leaves condensation on the inside of the vents.

That damp film catches dust, pet dander, and pollen. Together they are the conditions mold, mildew, and bacteria need. Every time the system starts, it can push that air into every room of a condo or townhouse.
If you already notice the smell, start with [air duct cleaning in Arlington, VA](/locations/arlington) rather than masking it with fresheners.

sections.heading: Why condos and older Arlington homes are at higher risk
paragraphs: High-rises along the river stack units, shared corridors, and long dryer runs. Ground floors and older brick houses in Lyon Village, Cherrydale, and along Columbia Pike often lack the tight vapor barriers of a new build, so outdoor humidity reaches basements, crawl spaces, and wall cavities more easily.
Once mold is in those hidden spots or in older ductwork, the blower spreads spores whenever heat or AC turns on. Households usually notice:
listItems: A persistent musty or earthy odor that does not leave when you open a window.
Dust that returns to furniture and registers within days of cleaning.
Allergy flare-ups, coughing, or watery eyes that are worse indoors than outside.

sections.heading: Why Arlington’s river climate shows up inside the house
paragraphs: Living in Arlington, VA means the Potomac is never far away — Rosslyn and Crystal City sit on it, and the same humid air reaches Clarendon, Ballston, and Columbia Pike. You feel it walking outside. It is also sitting in the one place that should stay comfortable: the air moving through your ducts.
Here is how that climate strains an Arlington HVAC system, and what to do before musty air becomes a recurring problem.

If the odor is already in the vents, or dust keeps returning after you clean the registers, do not wait for it to spread through the building. We now include ventilation mold treatment with our Arlington work, alongside standard flat-rate cleaning.
listItems: Keep indoor humidity below 50%: A dehumidifier in a basement, utility closet, or damp ground-floor room removes the water mold needs.
Keep dryer vents clear: A clogged line pushes moist air back into the laundry area. Full-length cleaning restores exhaust flow and cuts fire risk.
Inspect before the smell becomes normal: Professional cleaning plus photos shows whether the problem is dust, moisture, or both.
